These compounds are likely modulators of the G protein-coupled receptor pathway, which may influence the activity of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential role for androstenedione in modulating the expression or activity of UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4 through the activation of G protein-coupled receptors, possibly via the release of signaling molecules that influence enzyme expression. The evidence supports a mechanism where androstenedione indirectly affects UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B4 through a chain of targets, emphasizing the importance of receptor activation in this regulatory process.
